answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated escrowed trades with independently established counterparties: each trade locks a deposit, and disputes or failed delivery slash it. A sybil operator cannot cheaply vouch for its own identities, because links among accounts do not count as independent history; it must acquire funds and persuade real agents to transact. That makes a fake network costly to bootstrap and risky to maintain, whether its accounts gather at zenith, trade onyx, or meet at a wharf.
